ei.subject: 2025년 6월 고3 모의고사
ei.title: Laura and Cathy at the Farmer's Market

fullPassage:
(A) "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be (a) her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.

(B) Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Cathy, those peaches look delicious! I bought some blueberries. Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy happily. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, saying "(b) I really love this place! Thank you for the wonderful day."

(C) Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around. Are you ready?" Cathy answered excitedly, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!" The market was already crowded with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious to explore more, Cathy said, "While (c) you're buying jam, I'll look around the market and get some peaches."

(D) Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, (d) she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, (e) you'll have to wait another year for the season." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!" She bought two bags of peaches.

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, ①<u>waving</u> brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance ②<u>to buy</u> freshly-picked fruits. Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me ③<u>to show</u> you around." Cathy answered ④<u>excitedly</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ to show → show: let + 목적어 + 동사원형(사역동사). to부정사 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ to show → show: 사역동사 let + O + V원형. Let me show you around.
❌ ① waving: 분사구문(동시동작) — 정상
❌ ② to buy: a chance to V(to부정사 형용사적 용법) — 정상
❌ ④ excitedly: 동사(answered)를 수식하는 부사 — 정상
det.tip: 사역동사(let, make, have) + O + V원형. let me show (O) let me to show (X)

questions.passage: The market was already crowded with people of all ages. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious to explore more, Cathy said, "While you're buying jam, I'll look around the market." ①<u>Wandering</u> away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, ②<u>that</u> smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, she ③<u>picked</u> out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller ④<u>told</u> her they were a great choice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② that → which: 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법의 관계대명사는 which. that은 계속적 용법 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ ② that → which: 콤마(,) 뒤 관계대명사 계속적 용법 — that 사용 불가, which 필요
❌ ① Wandering: 분사구문(동시동작) — 정상
❌ ③ picked: picked out(골라냈다) 과거형 — 정상
❌ ④ told: told + 간접목적어(her) + 직접목적어(절) — 정상
det.tip: 관계대명사 계속적 용법: , which (O) / , that (X). 콤마 뒤에는 that 사용 불가

questions.passage: Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura ①<u>holding</u> a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Would you like to go to my place and ②<u>make</u> blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, ③<u>saying</u> she really loved this place. Born and raised in a big city where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy ④<u>has never had</u> a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits before this visit.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ has never had → had never had: 과거 시점(이사 전)까지의 경험이므로 과거완료.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ has never had → had never had: 과거 시점 이전의 경험 부정 → 과거완료(had + p.p.)
❌ ① holding: 지각동사(noticed) + O + -ing(현재분사) — 정상
❌ ② make: Would you like to go ... and make — 병렬구조(to + V원형) — 정상
❌ ③ saying: 분사구문(동시동작) — 정상
det.tip: 과거완료(had p.p.): 과거 시점 이전의 경험. had never had = (그 시점까지) 한 번도 ~한 적 없었다

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around." Cathy answered excitedly. The market was already ①<u>crowded</u> with people of all ages. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. ②<u>Curious</u> to explore more, Cathy said she would look around. Wandering away, Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled ③<u>awful</u>. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ④<u>ripe</u> peaches.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 신선한 꽃과 수제 비누 향기가 황홀했으므로 ③awful(끔찍한)은 부적절. 원문은 heavenly(천상의).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ awful(끔찍한) → 원문은 heavenly(천상의). 꽃과 비누 향기가 좋다는 문맥
❌ ① crowded(붐비는): 모든 연령대로 붐비는 시장 — 적절
❌ ② Curious(호기심 있는): 더 탐험하고 싶은 — 적절
❌ ④ ripe(잘 익은): 아름답고 잘 익은 복숭아 — 적절
det.tip: heavenly(천상의, 황홀한)↔awful(끔찍한): 향기에 대한 긍정/부정 표현

questions.passage: Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Cathy, those peaches look ①<u>delicious</u>! I bought some blueberries. Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy ②<u>happily</u>. As they walked out of the market, Cathy ③<u>criticized</u> her friend for the special experience, saying "I really love this place! Thank you for the ④<u>wonderful</u> day."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: Cathy는 특별한 경험에 감사했으므로 ③criticized(비판했다)는 부적절. 원문은 thanked(감사했다).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ criticized(비판했다) → 원문은 thanked(감사했다). 'I really love this place!'과 '비판'은 모순
❌ ① delicious(맛있는): 복숭아가 맛있어 보인다 — 적절
❌ ② happily(행복하게): 훌륭한 아이디어라며 행복하게 답함 — 적절
❌ ④ wonderful(멋진): 멋진 하루 — 적절
det.tip: thanked(감사했다)↔criticized(비판했다): 행동의 방향이 완전 반대

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great __________ because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, you'll have to wait another year for the season."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 한정 판매이므로 훌륭한 선택(choice)이라고 과일 판매자가 말했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② choice(선택): 원문 'a great choice' — 이번 주까지만이라 좋은 선택
❌ ① burden(부담): 긍정적 추천 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ risk(위험): 과일 구매에 위험은 부적합
❌ ④ problem(문제): 추천 문맥과 반대
det.tip: a great choice = 훌륭한 선택. 판매자가 구매를 추천하는 긍정적 표현

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables. As they walked out of the market later, Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, saying "I really love this place! Thank you for the __________day."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시장 경험에 감사하며 멋진(wonderful) 하루라고 표현했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① wonderful(멋진): 'I really love this place!' + 감사 = 긍정적 경험
❌ ② terrible(끔찍한): 사랑한다는 표현과 모순
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): special experience와 모순
❌ ④ boring(지루한): 신나서 달려가고 감사하는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: wonderful(멋진): love + thank → 긍정적 경험. 감정 단서로 빈칸 추론

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: Cathy는 대도시에서 태어나고 자랐다(Born and raised in a big city).
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문 'Born and raised in a big city' — 정확히 일치
❌ ① Cathy가 Laura's town으로 이사한 것이지 반대 아님
❌ ③ 'had never had a chance' — 처음이므로 자주 간 적 없음
❌ ④ 'her friend' — 이미 친구 사이
det.tip: Born and raised in a big city: 대도시 출신. recently moved into Laura's town: 최근 이사

questions.passage: Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around. Are you ready?" Cathy answered excitedly, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!" The market was already crowded with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 시장은 다양한 연령대의 사람들로 붐비고 있었다.
Laura는 판매 중인 딸기 잼을 발견했다.
Cathy가 Laura에게 딸기 잼을 사다 주었다.

det.korean: Laura가 직접 딸기 잼을 사러 간 것이지, Cathy가 사다 준 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 불일치: 원문 'Laura found ... She walked over to buy some' — Laura가 직접 구매
❌ ① 일치: 'Let me show you around'
❌ ② 일치: 'crowded with people of all ages'
❌ ③ 일치: 'Laura found some strawberry jam for sale'
det.tip: 주어 혼동 함정: Laura found and walked over to buy ≠ Cathy bought for Laura

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, you'll have to wait another year for the season." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!" She bought two bags of peaches.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Cathy는 신선한 꽃과 수제 비누 부스를 지나쳤다.
과일 판매자는 복숭아가 이번 주까지만 있다고 했다.

det.korean: Cathy는 '정말 싸다(really cheap)'고 했으므로 '비싸다고 생각했다'는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 불일치: 원문 'They're really cheap!' — 싸다고 했지 비싸다고 하지 않음
❌ ① 일치: 'walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps'
❌ ② 일치: 'they're only here until this week'
❌ ④ 일치: 'She bought two bags of peaches'
det.tip: cheap(싼)↔expensive(비싼): 원문의 정확한 표현을 확인. 'really cheap' ≠ 비싸다

questions.passage: (A) Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town and had never visited a farmer's market. (C) They entered the market together, and Cathy was excited. Laura found strawberry jam while Cathy explored. (D) Cathy found beautiful peaches and bought two bags after the seller told her they were seasonal. (B) They left the market, and Cathy expressed deep gratitude for the wonderful experience.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 친구와 함께한 첫 농산물 시장 방문의 즐거움

det.korean: 친구 Laura와 함께 처음 농산물 시장을 방문하여 즐거운 경험을 한 이야기.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 전체 글의 핵심: 친구와의 첫 시장 방문 → 탐험 → 구매 → 감사
❌ ① 시장 운영이 아닌 방문 경험
❌ ② 식생활 비교가 주제가 아님
❌ ④ 구매 방법이 아닌 경험 이야기
det.tip: 주제 = 인물의 행동과 감정 변화의 핵심. 기대→탐험→만족→감사

questions.passage: (A) Cathy, who had recently moved to Laura's town, was going to visit a farmer's market for the first time. Born in a big city with supermarkets, she had never bought freshly-picked produce. (C) At the market, she explored eagerly, finding it crowded and vibrant. (D) She discovered ripe peaches and learned they were seasonal, buying two bags. (B) After shopping, she thanked Laura, saying she loved the place and the wonderful day.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: The History of Farmer's Markets in Big Cities
How to Choose the Best Seasonal Fruits
The Economic Impact of Local Farmers
A City Girl's Delightful First Visit to a Farmer's Market

det.korean: 대도시 소녀의 첫 농산물 시장 방문 — 즐거운 경험.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 핵심 내용 반영: 대도시 출신(City Girl) + 첫 방문(First Visit) + 즐거움(Delightful)
❌ ① 역사가 아닌 개인 경험 이야기
❌ ② 과일 선택법이 아닌 경험 이야기
❌ ③ 경제적 영향이 아닌 개인 경험
det.tip: 제목 = 핵심 키워드 조합. City Girl + First Visit + Farmer's Market + Delightful

questions.passage: The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, you'll have to wait another year for the season." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!" She bought <u>two bags</u> of peaches.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 two bags가 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Cathy가 너무 많이 사서 후회하고 있다.
Cathy가 복숭아에 대해 매우 만족하여 적극적으로 구매했다.
Cathy가 Laura를 위해 선물을 준비하고 있다.

det.korean: 한 봉지에서 두 봉지로 늘린 것은 복숭아에 대한 높은 만족감과 적극적 구매 의사를 보여준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 'I'll get some more'(더 사겠다) + 'really cheap'(정말 싸다) + 'two bags' = 만족감
❌ ① 후회가 아닌 적극적 추가 구매
❌ ③ Laura를 위한 것이라는 근거 없음
❌ ④ 할인 언급 없음 — cheap은 원래 가격이 싸다는 뜻
det.tip: 함축의미: 행동(두 봉지 구매) + 발화(더 사겠다, 정말 싸다) = 높은 만족감의 표현

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be (a) <u>her</u> first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (a) her가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (a) her는 Cathy를 가리킨다. Laura의 마을로 이사한 Cathy의 첫 경험.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Cathy: 바로 앞 문장 'Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town' — Cathy의 첫 경험
❌ ② Laura: Laura는 이미 그 마을에 살고 있어 첫 경험이 아님
❌ ③ the fruit seller: 아직 등장하지 않음
❌ ④ Cathy's mother: 글에 등장하지 않음
det.tip: 대명사 지칭: 'Cathy had recently moved ... this was going to be her first experience' — her = Cathy

questions.passage: Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around. Are you ready?" Cathy answered excitedly. The market was already crowded with people of all ages. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious to explore more, Cathy said, "While (c) <u>you</u>'re buying jam, I'll look around the market and get some peaches."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (c) you가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (c) you는 Laura를 가리킨다. Cathy가 Laura에게 말하는 대화.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Laura: Cathy가 Laura에게 말하는 대화이므로 you = Laura. Laura가 잼을 사러 간 상황
❌ ① Cathy: Cathy가 말하는 주체이므로 you가 될 수 없음
❌ ③ the fruit seller: 아직 등장하지 않은 인물
❌ ④ the jam seller: 직접적 대화 상대 아님
det.tip: 대화 속 you: 말하는 사람(Cathy)이 듣는 사람(Laura)을 가리킴

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, you'll have to wait another year for the season." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!" She bought two bags of peaches.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

Cathy는 과일 가판대에서 아름답고 잘 익은 복숭아를 골랐는데, 꽃과 비누의 향기는 __________ 했다.
accept: heavenly
Heavenly
heavenly.

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.
